newsitem.title: UK: Ladbroke sees further good progress.
newsitem.headline: Ladbroke sees further good progress.

text.p: Ladbroke Group Plc Thursday posted a 34 percent increase in 1996 pretax profits to 163 million pounds ($263 million) before exceptional items and forecast further progress during 1997.
Chief executive Peter George also made positive remarks about trading since its 1996 year ended on December 31.

"The same trend has continued in the last two months. The businesses are doing well. It does seem to be getting gradually better this year in mainland Europe," George said in an interview. Trading profits from its European hotels fell slightly in 1996.
Revenue per available room in hotels in mainland Europe fell to 50.8 pounds ($81.94) in 1996 from 52.1 pounds ($84.03). In London it rose to 70.4 ($113.55) pounds from 60.4 ($97.42).
Overall hotel occupancy levels rose slightly to 69.6 percent from 69 percent and group revenue per available room from 48 pounds ($77.42) to 49.3 pounds ($79.52).
Ladbroke shares gained 10p to reach 235p in morning trade as the company's profit figure exceeded the consensus forecast from brokers of 160 million pounds ($258 million).

"The results were a little better than our expectations at both the pretax and the earnings per share level," said Nigel Reed, industry analyst at Paribas Capital Markets. Earnings per share before exceptional items were up 40 percent to 10.44 pence during the period.

Hilton International, which operates Hilton hotels outside the United States, increased trading profits by an underlying 20 percent to 160.2 million ($258 million), and the betting and gaming division grew profits by 46 percent to 84.9 million ($136.9 million).
